title: Ben Derusai
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: The sages commonly use the expression “like the food of Ben Derusai,” as in Shabbat 20a. He was a bandit who ate his food when it was only one-third cooked. So too in Avodah Zarah, chapter 2, at the beginning of halakhah 9.[^1][^2]

notes.text: רה״ט is read as “at the beginning of halakhah 9.” The one-third cooking measure is retained as Hyman gives it.

Shabbat 20a uses “the food of Ben Derusai,” and the checked Rashi gloss calls him a bandit and gives one-third cooking. Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah 2:9 also uses the expression. Hyman’s locator רה״ט is rendered as the beginning of halakhah 9; the passage comparison does not add a historical identification or a legal ruling.
